pageCache.pageTitle: About Us - Welcome to Cheam Common Juniors Academy
pageCache.text:
About Us
At Cheam Common Junior Academy we aim to encourage and develop the potential of our pupils to the full. The starting point will vary from child to child and each pupil is encouraged to progress and meet challenges appropriate to his or her abilities.
On leaving the school, we are confident that our children will have retained their curiosity, acquired a great deal of knowledge, will have developed a learning code and will be keen to continue with their studies.
Pupils at Cheam Common Junior Academy benefit from a wide range of facilities. These include 1:1 Chromebooks, a library, sensory rooms, inclusion hub, inovation hub, pupil leadership room, multi-use games area and a forest school area.
PedTech Impact Report
At Cheam Common Junior Academy we are committed to using technology to develop teaching and learning. Please watch the video that shows the findings of our recent PedTech Impact Report.
For more information, please see the PedTech page on the LEO Academy Trust Website

pageCache.pageTitle: LEO Academy Trust - Welcome to Cheam Common Juniors Academy
pageCache.text:
LEO Academy Trust
Our Mission
LEO Academy Trust is committed to developing a family of great schools, where collaboration makes a real difference for our children, staff and communities.
Our Vision
Learning Excellence Opportunity
Great Learning communities; Excellence for all; endless Opportunity.
Cheam Common Junior Academy is a proud member of the LEO Academy Trust. LEO Academy Trust is committed to ensuring that all its schools are provided with the same amazing opportunities and that pupils are valued across the Trust.
At Cheam Common Junior Academy, the support and guidance from LEO Academy Trust significantly contributes to our commitment to excellence in education. Together, we strive to create an environment where every child is empowered to succeed academically, socially, and emotionally. The partnership between our school and LEO Academy Trust underscores our dedication to providing the highest quality education and ensuring a bright future for all our students.
The Trust prides itself on offering a wide range of extra-curricular activities and varied opportunities for all pupils. LEO believes that school is about so much more than learning how to read and write, and endeavours to provide pupils with opportunities that they may not have exposure to in everyday life.
All pupils participate in the Trust’s 1:1 Chromebook Programme. Equipped with their own devices, pupils are able to engage more deeply in their learning and independently select the resources they need to enhance their education. LEO’s Pupil Outcomes encourage our pupils to be innovative learners who pursue excellence; developing digital skills and maximising the use of technology in their learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: LEO Explorers - Welcome to Cheam Common Juniors Academy
pageCache.text:
LEO Explorers
LEO Academy Trust, prides itself in developing the whole child and preparing them for the next stage of their learning. We aim to develop well-rounded pupils who develop critical thinking, leadership skills, life skills and cultural capital.
This is supported through our LEO Explorer Characteristics which underpin our curriculum, empowering all pupils to embrace our LEO Pupil Outcomes.
Creating a positive and inclusive classroom environment is fundamental to the development of LEO Explorer Characteristics. We believe that by nurturing these attributes and attitudes for learning, we equip our pupils to be confident, compassionate, and capable leaders who positively impact their communities and help shape a better tomorrow.
LEO Explorer Characteristic Child Definitions
The creation of LEO explorer characteristics has been a fabulous collaboration of thoughts and ideas from a number of groups from within the LEO Team. Special thanks to everyone involved in this project with particular recognition to Niamh Wilson for bringing the LEO explorers to life with her brilliant illustrations and Evo Hannan for getting us started on this journey.

pageCache.pageTitle: Modern Foreign Languages - Welcome to Cheam Common Juniors Academy
pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages
Learning a foreign language is a liberation from insularity and provides an opening to other cultures. At Cheam Common Junior Academy, we aim to provide a high-quality language programme that fosters children’s curiosity and deepens their understanding of the world. Our curriculum enables children to express their ideas and thoughts in another language and understand and respond to its speakers, both in speech and in writing. We provide opportunities for children to communicate for practical purposes, learn new ways of thinking and read in the original language. Our teaching of language aims to provide the foundation for learning further languages, in order to equip our children to study and work in other countries.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music - Welcome to Cheam Common Juniors Academy
pageCache.text:
Music
At Cheam Common Junior Academy, we believe that music making is a powerful and personal experience that can aid children’s development in so many ways; academically, physically, socially and emotionally. Our aim is to provide every child with a high quality music education which engages, inspires and nurtures a love of music and so in turn, increases self confidence, creativity and achievement.
We are committed to providing the children with a wide variety of learning activities that include performing, composing, listening and appraising a wide variety of music from different genres, eras and cultures. Our children have the opportunity to play at least one instrument whilst they are at Cheam Common and will be able to develop an understanding and use different forms of music notation. We offer extensive range of enrichment activities which includes trips, visitors, choir, rock band, performing in high quality musical events and productions and playing in our orchestra. We deliver our Music Curriculum through the 'Sing Up' scheme of work and in collaboration with Sutton Music Service.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maths and Financial Literacy - Welcome to Cheam Common Juniors Academy
pageCache.text:
Maths and Financial Literacy
Maths
Mathematics is a creative and highly interconnected discipline that has been developed over centuries, providing the solution to some of history’s most intriguing problems. It is essential to everyday life, critical to science, technology and engineering, and necessary for financial literacy and most forms of employment. At Cheam Common, we provide a high-quality mathematics education that provides a foundation for understanding the world, the ability to reason mathematically, an appreciation of the beauty and power of mathematics, and a sense of enjoyment and curiosity about the subject.
At Cheam Common, we follow the Maths No Problem scheme of work. We also incorporate high-quality mathematical resources from other providers into our lessons to provide children with opportunities to reason and problem solve, including NCETM and White Rose.
National Curriculum: Maths KS1 and KS2
Year 3 Transition to NCETM
Here at CCJ, we continually review and adapt our curriculum to ensure we offer the best possible learning experience for our children.
From this academic year, Year 3 will be transitioning to the NCETM (National Centre for Excellence in the Teaching of Mathematics) approach for Maths, moving away from Maths — No Problem! (MNP).
Why We Made This Decision
This change was made as a local, school-based decision focused on continuity and progression for our children:
Building on Familiar Foundations: Our Year 3 pupils successfully used the NCETM framework throughout Key Stage 1 (Year 1 and Year 2). Transitioning Year 3 to NCETM aligns their learning with the familiar structures, representations, and vocabulary they experienced in earlier year groups.
Consistency in Learning: By aligning Year 3 with Key Stage 1, we ensure a smoother academic transition as children step into Key Stage 2.
Mastery Approach: NCETM materials are designed around a "Teaching for Mastery" model, which breaks concepts down into small, coherent steps so every child can build a deep, lasting understanding of mathematical principles.
Learn More About NCETM
If you would like to find out more about the framework, its resources, or how maths is taught using this approach, you can visit the NCETM Website.

Maths Progression Map
We have also incorporated useful digital manipulatives that are often used in lessons, including Polipad (Mathigon) and MathsBot.
We encourage children to use Times Tables Rockstars and Century for 30 minutes a week for their home learning. Parent guides to these websites can be found by clicking the links above.
Financial Literacy
At Cheam Common, we teach the skills, knowledge, attitudes and behaviours that help people to manage money and achieve good financial wellbeing begin to develop from an early age. Research shows that financial behaviour starts to be shaped between the ages of three and seven, and long-term financial outcomes can be predicted from skills and behaviour in children as young as five.
Financial Literacy lessons take place once per half term.

pageCache.text:
Sport & PE
Our vision for school PE, Sport and physical activities is to ensure that we promote and support the importance of a healthy lifestyle and place particular emphasis on the wellbeing of our pupils and how this impacts positively on all aspects of school life. All our work will be aimed at increasing attainment, participation, improving confidence and skills and encouraging a life-long love of sport and physical activities together with an understanding of the health benefits that participation offers.
